newsitem.title: USA: Heavy storms hit Iowa, brief heat wave on the way.
newsitem.headline: Heavy storms hit Iowa, brief heat wave on the way.

text.p: A storm that ripped through central Iowa early Thursday was expected to move northeast, bringing chances for rain in the northwest Corn Belt through Saturday, meteorologists said.

"The next three nights and mornings we are going to have chances for rain favoring the northwest Corn Belt, 0.50 to 2.00 inches with 40 to 50 percent coverage each of the next three nights," Weather Express Inc Chief Forecaster Fred Gesser said.
Unofficial reports showed the storm dumped more than four inches of rain in Des Moines in four hours, he said.
A heat wave was expected to move into the U.S. Midwest behind the storm, bringing temperatures above 90 degrees Fahrenheit from Nebraska to Indiana.

Temperatures were expected to peak in the mid-90s in Nebraska, Missouri and southwest Illinois on Friday and Saturday, with low 90s expected in Peoria, Illinois, said Joel Burgio, meteorologist with Weather Services Corp.
But Burgio said long-range forecasts showed showers and cooler temperatures would reach the Corn Belt by Monday as a front moved across the region.
"This is going to increase the chances for showers and that should spell the end of the hot, dry spell," Burgio said.
Temperatures were expected to drop to below normal by the middle of next week, Burgio said.
Beyond that, Gesser said another warm-up would occur by the end of July with the next rain event likely to reach the western Corn Belt on August 2.
